newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - March 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

A poll by Opinion Research Business has put support for Labour at 53 per cent, leaving John Major's Conservatives trailing behind on 29 per cent. The Tories have lost a further 5 points to Labour, while the Lib Dems have remained at 12 per cent.
THE POUND STAYS ON A LOSING STREAK

Sterling continued to fall on the foreign exchange markets overnight, following news of sluggish manufacturing data. The weak figures added weight to the argument that British interest rates do not need to rise to curb inflationary pressures. Also damaging to the pound was a statement from the British Embassy in Tokyo that Howard Davies, Deputy Governor of the Bank of England, had been misquoted yesterday. Davies had been reported as saying sterling was too high against the German mark, but it now seems he said the markets had perceived sterling as too high.
RING OF STEEL CUTS CITY CRIME BY 15 PERCENT

Reported crime committed in the City of London fell by 15 percent in 1996. The biggest factor in this was the ring of steel, introduced in 1992-3 in the wake of IRA bombings, in addition to an increase in the number of policemen on the beat and surveillance cameras.
GENERAL CABLE TUNES IN TO COMCAST TALKS

General Cable, the cable TV and telecommunications group, has held takeover talks with Comcast UK, which could lead to more consolidation in the British cable industry following last year's announcement by Cable & Wireless that its subsidiary Mercury will be merged with three cable companies to create Cable & Wireless Communications (CWC). General Cable and Comcast combined could be attractive to a larger predator like Telewest, or even the proposed CWC.
